disease_label: Rett syndrome (congenital/atypical and classical RTT); patient 1 severe RTT-like neurodevelopmental disorder, patient 2 classical RTT
moi: AD (autosomal dominant, haploinsufficiency; both variants de novo). Note: FOXG1 is autosomal, not X-linked.
source_title: Phenotypic variability in Rett syndrome associated with FOXG1 mutations in females

variants.domain: Truncation removes both GBD (Groucho-binding domain) and JBD (JARID1B-binding domain). Note: results text states c.924A>G; Figure 1A legend states c.924G>A (discrepancy in source).
More carboxy-terminal truncation; retains intact GBD, may retain residual repression activity

expected_evidence.value: Postnatal/acquired microcephaly (head growth deceleration); Developmental delay / no acquisition of speech; Loss/absence of purposeful hand skills; Hand stereotypies; Severe epilepsy with hyperthermia-induced seizures and myoclonic seizures (patient 1); Strabismus; Feeding/swallowing difficulties; Global hypotonia; Foot deformity (equinovarus); Choreic movements; Sialorrhoea / drooling; Bruxism; Inappropriate episodes of laughing; Autistic behaviour with poor eye contact (patient 2); Ataxia (patient 2); Self-abusive behaviour (patient 2); Hemihypotrophy of left body (patient 2); Bone fractures suggestive of osteoporosis (patient 1); Brain malformations: ventricular enlargement, corpus callosum hypoplasia, decreased white matter, paucity of gyral development (patient 1); Facial dysmorphism: protruding ears, anteverted nostrils, open mouth (patient 2)
Patient 1: ~4 months (head growth deceleration noted at 2 months); Patient 2: ~6 months
